Calidad del dato y contexto: Lo primero: Data quality and context: The first thing was to check the health of the data. We look for null values ​​or empty cells, since that would have forced us to impute data using the mean of the variables. Luckily, the dataset was pristine, with no missing values, which gave us a very solid base to start with. However, the data lacks competitive context. To solve this, we cross-reference player information with external dictionaries to place each player in their corresponding league. In addition, we added the Opta Power Ranking (September 2023). This was key: scoring 10 goals in the Premier League is not the same as in a minor league. "The Opta Power Rankings assess and rate more than 15,000 men's and women's domestic teams across the globe on advanced performance metrics. Each team receives a score on a global scale, from 0 (the weakest) to 100 (the strongest)." This is key, scoring 10 goals in the Premier League is not the same as scoring 10 goals in a minor league. Thanks to this coefficient, the model can understand the real merit of each statistic depending on where it was produced.

LASSO (Enfoque Explicativo y Selección): LASSO (Explanatory and Selection Approach) Given the high correlation between variables (e.g. minutes played and matches), the simple linear regression suffered from multicollinearity. We chose LASSO because it solves this automatically: it penalizes and eliminates redundant variables (noise), leaving only the significant ones. It gives us transparency, it allows us to see the exact formula of the market.

Lista de Infravalorados: El modelo ident: Undervalued List: The model identifies world elite veterans (Messi, Lewandowski, Benzema) as great market opportunities. While the financial market penalizes its price due to its lack of future resale capacity (depreciation due to age), the model values ​​its Immediate Return (ROIC). Statistically, these players produce offensive figures much higher than their current market value, being ideal assets for clubs seeking short-term sporting performance without prioritizing financial gain.
Lista de Sobrevalorados: Inversamente, l: Overrated List: Conversely, the list of theoretically “overrated” players is full of young talents (Bellingham, Pedri, Gavi). The real market assigns prices greater than €100M based on the Expected Future Value (Potential). However, the model, based strictly on current statistical reality, considers it inefficient to pay such sums for players who, to this day, have not yet accumulated the volume of goals and assists of established stars. Furthermore, most of these players are not center forwards, only oshimen is, through simple variables such as goals or assists, it is difficult to measure players like Pedri, with an amazing impact on the game, controlling the time of the game, but without finisher numbers.

Log prices reduce the scale imbalance; a: The logarithmic transformation allows me to work with a very unequal price scale and evaluate the estimates in a reserved sample.
Los coeficientes estimados miden el impa: The estimated coefficients measure the marginal impact of the variables on the value of the players, keeping the rest constant, as the variable is on a logarithmic scale, it measures estimated percentage changes. We see that age has a positive coefficient, but the quadratic age has a negative one, correcting the former when the player reaches his maturity stage, these two coefficients must be interpreted together. As for minutes, its coefficient is lower since the values ​​taken by minutes played, the range, are much higher. The positive league coefficient means that playing in a more prestigious league, with a higher coefficient, boosts a player's market value. The same thing happens with prizes.
Los datos originales venían promediados: The original data was averaged over 90 minutes. This is dangerous. Imagine a substitute playing the last 10 minutes of the season and scoring a rebound goal. Tras analizar las limitaciones de los mo: After analyzing the limitations of linear models, which assume constant and proportional relationships, we made a methodological leap towards algorithms capable of capturing the real complexity of the market: tree-based methods. A decision tree is, in essence, a set of chained logical rules, similar to a flowchart. The algorithm repeatedly divides the data set into increasingly homogeneous subgroups based on binary (Yes/No) questions about the variables. However, individual trees have a major flaw: they are unstable and prone to overfitting. They memorize training data too well, but fail to predict new data. A small change to the dataset can radically change the structure of the tree.
